units.zh: 康延孝，塞北部落人也。
units.en: Kang Yanxiao came from the northern frontier tribes.
units.literal: Kang Yanxiao was a man of the northern frontier tribes.

units.zh: 初隸太原，因得罪，亡命於汴梁。
units.en: He first served under Taiyuan; after committing an offense he fled to Bianliang.
units.literal: At first he was subordinated to Taiyuan; having offended, he fled his life to Bianliang.

units.zh: 開平、乾化中，自隊長積勞至部校。
units.en: During the Kaiping and Qianhua reigns he worked his way up from squad leader to company commander.
units.literal: During Kaiping and Qianhua, through accumulated service he rose from squad leader to company commander.

units.zh: 梁末帝時，頻立軍功。
units.en: Under the Last Emperor of Liang he won military honors again and again.
units.literal: Under Liang's Last Emperor, he repeatedly won military merit.

units.zh: 同光元年八月，段凝率眾五萬營於王村，時延孝為右先鋒指揮使，率百騎來奔。
units.en: In the eighth month of Tongguang 1, Duan Ning camped at Wang Village with fifty thousand men. Yanxiao, then Right Vanguard Commander, came over with a hundred riders.
units.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Tongguang, Duan Ning led fifty thousand troops and encamped at Wang Village; at that time Yanxiao was Right Vanguard Commander and led a hundred horsemen to defect.

units.zh: 莊宗得之，喜，解禦衣金帶以賜之。
units.en: Zhuangzong welcomed him gladly, stripped off his own imperial robe and gold belt, and gave them to him.
units.literal: Zhuangzong received him, rejoiced, and removed his imperial robe and gold belt to bestow them on him.

units.zh: 翌日，賜田宅於鄴，以為捧日軍使兼南面招討指揮使、檢校司空，守博州刺史。
units.en: The next day he granted him fields and a house at Ye and made him commander of the Sun-Rising Army, southern-route pacification commander, acting Sikong, and defender of Bo Prefecture.
units.literal: The next day he bestowed fields and a residence at Ye, appointing him commander of the Sun-Rising Army and simultaneous southern-route pacification commander, acting Sikong, and defender of Bo Prefecture.

units.zh: 莊宗屏人問梁兵機，延孝備陳利害，語在《莊宗紀》中。
units.en: Zhuangzong sent everyone else away and asked about Liang's military situation. Yanxiao laid out the pros and cons in full; the account appears in the "Annals of Zhuangzong."
units.literal: Zhuangzong dismissed attendants and questioned him on Liang military affairs; Yanxiao fully set forth advantages and disadvantages—the account is in the "Annals of Zhuangzong."

units.zh: 莊宗平汴，延孝頗有力焉，以功授檢校太保、鄭州防禦使，賜姓，名紹琛。
units.en: When Zhuangzong took Bian, Yanxiao had done much to help. For his service he was made acting Grand Guardian and Zhengzhou defense commissioner and granted the surname with the name Shaochen.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Bian, Yanxiao contributed considerably; for his merit he was appointed acting Grand Guardian and Zhengzhou defense commissioner, granted the surname with the name Shaochen.

units.zh: 明年，郊禮畢，授保義軍節度使。
units.en: The following year, after the suburban sacrifices, he was appointed military commissioner of the Baoyi Army.
units.literal: The next year, after the suburban rites were completed, he was appointed military commissioner of the Baoyi Army.

units.zh: 三年，討蜀，以延孝為西南行營馬步軍先鋒、排陣斬斫等使。
units.en: In the third year of the campaign against Shu, Yanxiao was appointed vanguard of the Southwest Campaign Army's horse and foot forces and commissioner for battle formation and close combat.
units.literal: In the third year, when Shu was attacked, Yanxiao was made vanguard of the cavalry and infantry of the Southwest Campaign Army and commissioner for array deployment and cutting down the enemy.

units.zh: 延孝性驍健，徇利奮不顧身。
units.en: Yanxiao was fierce and hardy by nature, and greedy for profit; in battle he threw himself forward without thought for his own life.
units.literal: Yanxiao was by nature fierce and hardy; greedy for gain, he fought without regard for his own body.

units.zh: 以前鋒下鳳州，收固鎮，降興州，敗王衍軍於三泉，所俘蜀軍皆諭而釋之，自是晝夜兼行。
units.en: Leading the vanguard, he took Feng Prefecture, seized Gu Town, accepted the surrender of Xing Prefecture, and routed Wang Yan's army at Sanquan. Every Shu soldier taken captive was reasoned with and then set free. From that point he pressed on day and night without pause.
units.literal: As vanguard he took Feng Prefecture, seized Gu Town, received the surrender of Xing Prefecture, and defeated Wang Yan's army at Sanquan; all captured Shu soldiers were admonished and released, and from then on he marched day and night without rest.

units.zh: 王衍自利州奔歸成都，斷吉柏津浮梁，以絕諸軍。
units.en: Wang Yan fled from Lizhou to Chengdu, destroyed the pontoon bridge at Jibai Ford, and thereby severed the route of the invading armies.
units.literal: Wang Yan fled from Lizhou back to Chengdu, cut the pontoon bridge at Jibai Ford, and thereby cut off the armies.

units.zh: 延孝復造浮梁以渡，進收綿州，王衍復斷綿江浮梁而去。
units.en: Yanxiao built another pontoon bridge and crossed, then advanced to take Mian Prefecture. Wang Yan once more destroyed the pontoon bridge on the Mian River and withdrew.
units.literal: Yanxiao again built a pontoon bridge to cross, advanced and took Mian Prefecture, and Wang Yan again cut the pontoon bridge on the Mian River and withdrew.

units.zh: 水深無舟楫可渡，延孝謂招撫使李嚴曰：「吾懸軍深入，利在急兵。
units.en: The river was too deep and there were no boats to ferry them across. Yanxiao said to the pacification commissioner Li Yan, "We have driven a detached force deep into enemy country. Our advantage lies in striking fast.
units.literal: The water was deep and there were no boats or rafts by which to cross. Yanxiao said to the pacification commissioner Li Yan: "I have led an isolated army deep into enemy territory; the advantage lies in pressing the attack swiftly.

units.zh: 乘王衍破膽之時，人心離沮，但得百騎過鹿頭關，彼即迎降不暇。
units.en: While Wang Yan is still shaken and his men are losing heart, even a hundred horsemen who get through Deer Head Pass will find the enemy too busy surrendering to resist us.
units.literal: While Wang Yan's courage is broken and men's hearts are divided and discouraged, if only a hundred horsemen can pass Deer Head Pass, the enemy will have no leisure but to welcome us in surrender.

units.zh: 如俟修繕津梁，便留數日，若王衍堅閉近關，折吾兵勢，儻延旬浹，則勝負莫可知也，宜促騎渡江。」
units.en: If we wait to repair the bridge and lose several days, and Wang Yan seals the passes nearby and blunts our momentum, then in ten days' time no one can say who will win. We must get the cavalry across the river immediately."
units.literal: If we wait to repair the ford bridge and stay several days, and Wang Yan firmly closes the nearby passes and breaks our army's momentum, and if it drags on for ten days, then victory and defeat cannot be known; we should urge the cavalry to cross the river at once."

units.zh: 因與李嚴乘馬浮江，於是得濟者僅千人，步軍溺死者亦千餘人。
units.en: He and Li Yan then rode their horses across the swollen river. Only about a thousand men made it over; more than a thousand foot soldiers drowned.
units.literal: Thereupon he and Li Yan rode their horses across the river floating; thus only about a thousand men got across, and more than a thousand foot soldiers drowned.

units.zh: 延孝既濟，長驅通鹿頭，進據漢州。
units.en: Once across, Yanxiao drove hard through Deer Head Pass and seized Han Prefecture.
units.literal: Once Yanxiao had crossed, he drove straight through to Deer Head and advanced to occupy Han Prefecture.

units.zh: 居三日，部下後軍方至。
units.en: Three days passed before the rest of his army caught up.
units.literal: After three days, the rear units of his subordinates finally arrived.

units.zh: 偽蜀六軍使王宗弼令人持牛酒幣馬歸款。
units.en: Wang Zongbi, commander of the Six Armies of the Shu regime, sent envoys with cattle, wine, silks, and horses to offer surrender.
units.literal: The bogus-Shu Six Armies commissioner Wang Zongbi sent men bearing cattle, wine, silks, and horses to submit.

units.zh: 旬日，兩川平定，延孝止漢州以俟繼岌。
units.en: Within ten days both the eastern and western circuits of Shu were pacified. Yanxiao held Han Prefecture to await Prince Siji.
units.literal: Within ten days the Two Chuan were pacified; Yanxiao halted at Han Prefecture to await Siji.

units.zh: 平蜀之功，延孝居最。
units.en: Of all who had helped conquer Shu, Yanxiao's achievement stood foremost.
units.literal: In the merit of pacifying Shu, Yanxiao ranked first.

units.zh: 時邠州節度使董璋為行營右廂馬步使，華州節度使毛璋為行營左廂馬步使，以軍禮當事延孝。
units.en: At the time Dong Zhang, military governor of Bin, served as right-wing horse-and-foot commander of the campaign army, and Mao Zhang, military governor of Hua, as left-wing commander. By military protocol both should have deferred to Yanxiao.
units.literal: At that time the military governor of Bin Prefecture Dong Zhang was right-wing cavalry and infantry commander of the campaign army, and the military governor of Hua Prefecture Mao Zhang was left-wing cavalry and infantry commander; by military etiquette they should have deferred to Yanxiao.

units.zh: 郭崇韜以私愛董璋，及西川平定之後，崇韜每有兵機，必召璋參決，延孝不平。
units.en: Guo Chongtao favored Dong Zhang personally. After western Sichuan was pacified, Chongtao consulted Zhang on every military matter, which rankled Yanxiao.
units.literal: Guo Chongtao favored Dong Zhang out of personal affection, and after the western Sichuan pacification, whenever Chongtao had military decisions he always summoned Zhang to deliberate; Yanxiao was resentful.

units.zh: 時延孝軍於城西，毛璋軍於城東，董璋軍於城中。
units.en: Yanxiao's troops camped west of the city, Mao Zhang's east of it, and Dong Zhang's inside the walls.
units.literal: At that time Yanxiao's army was west of the city, Mao Zhang's east of the city, and Dong Zhang's inside the city.

units.zh: 閏十二月，延孝因酒酣謂董璋曰：「吾有平蜀之功，公等仆蔌相從，反首鼠於侍中之門，謀相傾陷，吾為都將，公乃裨校，力能斬首。」
units.en: In the intercalary twelfth month, Yanxiao, deep in his cups, said to Dong Zhang, "I won Shu. You tagged along behind me like lackeys, yet you play both sides at the Chief Councilor's door and plot my ruin. I am the chief commander and you a mere subordinate — I could take your head whenever I chose."
units.literal: In the intercalary twelfth month, Yanxiao, flushed with wine, said to Dong Zhang: "I have the merit of pacifying Shu. You all followed me like menials, yet you play the fence-straddler at the Chief Councilor's gate and plot to overthrow me. I am the chief commander and you are only a subordinate officer — I have the strength to cut off your head."

units.zh: 璋惶恐，謝之而退。
units.en: Zhang was terrified, apologized, and withdrew.
units.literal: Zhang was fearful, apologized, and withdrew.

units.zh: 酒罷，璋訴於郭崇韜，崇韜陰銜之，乃署董璋為東川節度使，落軍職。
units.en: After the banquet Zhang complained to Guo Chongtao. Chongtao already bore a private grudge against Yanxiao and now appointed Dong Zhang military governor of Dongchuan, stripping him of his field command.
units.literal: When the drinking ended, Zhang complained to Guo Chongtao. Chongtao secretly harbored resentment toward Yanxiao and thereupon appointed Dong Zhang military governor of Dongchuan and removed him from military command.

units.zh: 延孝怒，謂毛璋曰：「吾冒白刃，犯險阻，平定兩川，董璋何功，遽有其地！」
units.en: Yanxiao flew into a rage and told Mao Zhang, "I faced naked steel and treacherous passes to conquer both circuits of Shu. What has Dong Zhang done to deserve that territory!"
units.literal: Yanxiao was angry and said to Mao Zhang: "I braved naked blades and dangerous passes and pacified the Two Chuan — what merit has Dong Zhang that he should suddenly receive that territory!"

units.zh: 二人因謁見崇韜，曰：「東川重地，宜擇良帥，工部任尚書有文武才幹，甚洽眾心，請表為東川帥。」
units.en: The two went to Chongtao and said, "Dongchuan is too important to leave in the wrong hands. Minister of Works Ren has civil and military ability and the full trust of the men. We ask that you recommend him as governor of Dongchuan."
units.literal: The two men thereupon had an audience with Chongtao and said: "Dongchuan is an important region and should have a worthy commander. Minister of Works Ren, the former Director of the Imperial Secretariat, has both civil and military talent and is greatly trusted by the troops. We ask that you memorialize him as commander of Dongchuan."

units.zh: 崇韜怒曰：「紹琛反耶？
units.en: Chongtao snapped, "Has Shaochen turned rebel?
units.literal: Chongtao said angrily: "Has Shaochen rebelled?

units.zh: 敢違吾節度！」
units.en: How dare he defy my orders!"
units.literal: He dares defy my command!"

units.zh: 延孝等惶恐而退。
units.en: Yanxiao and his companions withdrew in alarm.
units.literal: Yanxiao and the others withdrew in fear.

units.zh: 未幾，崇韜為繼岌所害，二人因責董璋曰：「公復首鼠何門？」
units.en: Before long Chongtao was killed on Siji's orders. The two men then turned on Dong Zhang. "Which door will you straddle now?" they demanded.
units.literal: Before long Chongtao was killed by Siji, and the two men thereupon reproached Dong Zhang, saying: "To which door will you play the fence-straddler now?"

units.zh: 璋俯首祈哀而已。
units.en: Zhang could only bow his head and plead for his life.
units.literal: Zhang only bowed his head and begged for mercy.

units.zh: 四年正月甲申，大軍發成都，繼岌令延孝以一萬二千人為後軍。
units.en: On the jiashen day of the first month of the fourth year, the main army marched out of Chengdu. Siji assigned Yanxiao twelve thousand men as the rear guard.
units.literal: On the jiashen day of the first month of the fourth year, the great army set out from Chengdu. Siji ordered Yanxiao to take twelve thousand men as the rear guard.

units.zh: 二月癸巳，中軍次武連，中使詔至，諭以西平王朱友謙有罪伏誅，命繼岌殺其子遂州節度使令德，延孝大驚。
units.en: On the guisi day of the second month the main force reached Wulian. An imperial messenger arrived with an edict: Zhu Youqian, Prince of Western Pacification, had been executed for treason, and Siji was ordered to kill his son Lingde, military governor of Suizhou. Yanxiao was stunned.
units.literal: On the guisi day of the second month the central army halted at Wulian. An imperial envoy arrived with an edict announcing that the Prince of Western Pacification Zhu Youqian had been executed for his crimes and ordering Siji to kill his son Lingde, military governor of Suizhou. Yanxiao was greatly shocked.

units.zh: 俄而董璋率兵之遂州，遇延孝不謁，延孝怒，謂諸校曰：「南平梁汴，西定巴邛，畫策之謀，始於郭公，而汗馬之勞，力摧強敵，即吾也。
units.en: Soon afterward Dong Zhang marched to Suizhou and, meeting Yanxiao on the road, failed to pay his respects. Yanxiao raged at his officers. "We pacified Liang and Bian in the south and secured Ba and Qiong in the west. Lord Guo drew up the plans, but the hard fighting and the breaking of strong enemies — that was my work.
units.literal: Soon Dong Zhang led troops to Suizhou and, meeting Yanxiao, did not pay a courtesy visit. Yanxiao was angry and said to the commanders: "Pacifying Liang and Bian in the south and securing Ba and Qiong in the west — the planning began with Lord Guo, but the sweat of battle and the crushing of strong enemies — that was me.

units.zh: 若以背偽歸國，犄角而成霸業，即西平王之功第一。
units.en: If merit lay in abandoning a false master for the true dynasty and helping from two sides to build the empire, then the Prince of Western Pacification deserved first place.
units.literal: If one speaks of turning from a false regime to serve the true state and coordinating from two sides to achieve hegemony, then the Prince of Western Pacification's merit was first.

units.zh: 西平與郭公皆以無罪赤族，歸朝之後，次當及我矣！」
units.en: The Prince of Western Pacification and Lord Guo were both wiped out though guilty of nothing. Once we are back at court, my turn will come next!"
units.literal: The Prince of Western Pacification and Lord Guo were both exterminated to the last for no crime; after returning to court, I will be next!"

units.zh: 丙申，延孝次劍州。
units.en: On the bingshen day Yanxiao reached Jian Prefecture.
units.literal: On the bingshen day Yanxiao reached Jian Prefecture.

units.zh: 時延孝部下皆鄜、延、河中舊將，焦武等知西平王被禍，兼誅令德，號哭軍門，訴於延孝曰：「西平無罪，二百口伏誅，河中舊將，無不從坐，某等必死矣！」
units.en: Yanxiao's officers were mostly veterans from Fu, Yan, and Hezhong. When Jiao Wu and the others learned of the Prince of Western Pacification's fate and Lingde's impending execution, they wept at the camp gate and pleaded with Yanxiao, "The Prince was innocent, yet two hundred of his kin were slaughtered. Every old officer from Hezhong will be implicated. We are as good as dead!"
units.literal: At that time Yanxiao's subordinates were all old generals from Fu, Yan, and Hezhong. Jiao Wu and others, learning that the Prince of Western Pacification had suffered disaster and that Lingde was also to be executed, wailed at the army gate and appealed to Yanxiao: "The Prince of Western Pacification was guiltless; two hundred of his household were put to death. Of the old Hezhong generals, none will escape implication — we are certain to die!"

units.zh: 時魏王繼岌到泥溪，延孝報繼岌云：「河中兵士號哭，欲為亂。」
units.en: Prince Siji had by then reached Nixi. Yanxiao sent word to him, "The Hezhong troops are wailing in the camp and are on the verge of mutiny."
units.literal: At that time Prince of Wei Siji had reached Nixi. Yanxiao reported to Siji: "The Hezhong soldiers are wailing and wish to mutiny."

units.zh: 丁酉，延孝至劍州，遂擁眾回，自稱西川節度、三川製置等使，以檄招諭蜀人，三日間，眾及五萬。
units.en: On the dingyou day Yanxiao reached Jian Prefecture, then turned his army around. He declared himself military governor of Xichuan and commissioner for the Three Rivers region, issued proclamations to rally the people of Shu, and within three days had gathered fifty thousand men.
units.literal: On the dingyou day Yanxiao reached Jian Prefecture, then led his troops back in revolt, styled himself military governor of Xichuan and commissioner for the administration of the Three Rivers, and issued proclamations to summon the people of Shu; within three days his forces reached fifty thousand.

units.zh: 己亥，繼岌至利州。
units.en: On the jihai day Siji reached Lizhou.
units.literal: On the jihai day Siji reached Lizhou.

units.zh: 是夜，守吉柏津使密告魏王曰：「得紹琛文字，令斷吉柏浮梁。」
units.en: That night the officer guarding Jibai Ford secretly warned the prince, "I have a written order from Shaochen to destroy the pontoon bridge at Jibai."
units.literal: That night the keeper of Jibai Ford secretly reported to the Prince of Wei: "I have obtained a document from Shaochen ordering the Jibai pontoon bridge to be cut."

units.zh: 繼岌懼，乃令梁漢顒以兵控吉柏津。
units.en: Alarmed, Siji sent Liang Hanyong with troops to seize control of the ford.
units.literal: Siji was afraid and thereupon ordered Liang Hanyong to take troops and secure Jibai Ford.

units.zh: 延孝已擁眾急趨西川，繼岌遣人馳書諭之。
units.en: Yanxiao was already driving west with his rebel host. Siji sent a fast courier with a letter urging him to submit.
units.literal: Yanxiao had already led his troops in haste toward western Sichuan. Siji sent a messenger at full speed with a letter to admonish him.

units.zh: 夜半，令監軍使李廷安召任圜，因署為副招討使。
units.en: At midnight he had the army supervisor Li Ting'an summon Ren Yuan and appointed him deputy pacification commissioner.
units.literal: At midnight he ordered the army supervisor Li Ting'an to summon Ren Yuan and thereupon appointed him deputy pacification commissioner.

units.zh: 令圜率兵七千騎，與都指揮使梁漢顒、監軍李廷安討之。
units.en: Yuan was to lead seven thousand cavalry, together with the chief commander Liang Hanyong and the supervisor Li Ting'an, against the rebel.
units.literal: He ordered Yuan to lead seven thousand horsemen, together with the chief commander Liang Hanyong and the supervisor Li Ting'an, to attack him.

units.zh: 辛丑，先令都將何建崇擊劍門，下之。
units.en: On the xinchou day he first sent the chief commander He Jianchong against Sword Gate, which fell.
units.literal: On the xinchou day he first ordered the chief commander He Jianchong to attack Sword Gate and take it.

units.zh: 甲寅，圜以大軍至漢州，延孝來逆戰，圜令董璋以東川懦卒當其鋒，伏精兵於其後，延孝擊退東川之兵，急追之，遇伏兵起，延孝敗，馳入漢州，閉壁不出。
units.en: On the jiayin day Yuan reached Han Prefecture with the main army. Yanxiao met him in battle. Yuan put Dong Zhang's weaker eastern-Sichuan troops in the path of the charge and hid elite forces behind them. Yanxiao broke the eastern-Sichuan line and pursued recklessly until the ambush sprang up. Defeated, he galloped into Han Prefecture and shut himself behind the walls.
units.literal: On the jiayin day Yuan arrived at Han Prefecture with the great army. Yanxiao came out to give battle. Yuan ordered Dong Zhang to place the weak troops of eastern Sichuan against the enemy's point, with elite troops hidden behind them. Yanxiao routed the eastern-Sichuan troops and pursued hotly; when the ambush rose, Yanxiao was defeated, galloped into Han Prefecture, and closed the walls without coming out.

units.zh: 西川孟知祥以兵二萬，與圜合勢攻之。
units.en: Meng Zhixiang of western Sichuan brought twenty thousand men and joined Yuan in a combined assault.
units.literal: Meng Zhixiang of western Sichuan brought twenty thousand troops and joined Yuan in combined attack.

units.zh: 〈（《九國誌·李延厚傳》：康延孝入漢州，知祥遣延厚率兵二千會李仁罕討之，將行，誓士卒曰：「今出師不三旬必破賊，乃立功圖賞之日也。
units.en: (According to the Annals of the Nine States, biography of Li Yanhou: When Kang Yanxiao seized Han Prefecture, Zhixiang sent Yanhou with two thousand men to join Li Renhan against him. Before marching, Yanhou swore to his troops, "We will break the rebels within thirty days. This is the day to win glory and rewards.
units.literal: (Annals of the Nine States, biography of Li Yanhou: When Kang Yanxiao entered Han Prefecture, Zhixiang sent Yanhou with two thousand troops to join Li Renhan in attacking him. About to set out, he swore to the soldiers: "On this campaign, within thirty days we shall certainly break the bandits — this is the day to win merit and seek reward.

units.zh: 士卒忠奮者立東廂，衰疾者立西廂，無自苦也。」
units.en: Let the loyal and eager stand on the east side, and the weak and sick on the west — spare yourselves needless hardship."
units.literal: Soldiers who are loyal and ardent, stand in the east wing; those who are weak or ill, stand in the west wing — do not afflict yourselves."

units.zh: 得請行者七百人，逐延孝西寨，斬首百餘級，竟拔其城。）〉
units.en: Seven hundred men stepped forward. They stormed Yanxiao's western camp, took more than a hundred heads, and at last captured the city.)〉
units.literal: Seven hundred men volunteered to go. They pursued Yanxiao's western camp, cut off more than a hundred heads, and finally stormed the city.)〉

units.zh: 漢州四面樹竹木為柵。
units.en: Han Prefecture was ringed with palisades of bamboo and timber on every side.
units.literal: On all four sides of Han Prefecture they planted bamboo and trees as palisades.

units.zh: 三月乙丑，圜陣於金雁橋，即率諸軍鼓噪而進，四面縱火，風焰亙空。
units.en: On the yichou day of the third month Yuan drew up his lines at Golden Goose Bridge, then led the army forward with drums and war cries. Fire was set on every side until flames and smoke blotted out the sky.
units.literal: On the yichou day of the third month Yuan formed battle lines at Golden Goose Bridge, then led the armies forward with drums and shouts, setting fire on all four sides until flames and wind filled the sky.

units.zh: 於是延孝危急，引騎出戰，遇陣於金雁橋，又敗之，以十數騎奔綿州；
units.en: Yanxiao, now desperate, led his cavalry out to fight, met the enemy again at Golden Goose Bridge, was beaten once more, and fled toward Mian Prefecture with only a dozen horsemen.
units.literal: Yanxiao was now in desperate straits, led his horsemen out to fight, met the battle line at Golden Goose Bridge, was again defeated, and fled toward Mian Prefecture with a dozen or so riders;

units.zh: 何建崇追及，擒之，任圜命載以檻車。
units.en: He Jianchong overtook and captured him. Ren Yuan had him loaded into a barred cart.
units.literal: He Jianchong overtook him, captured him, and Ren Yuan ordered him placed in a caged cart.

units.zh: 時孟知祥與任圜、董璋置酒高會，因引令延孝檻車至會。
units.en: Meng Zhixiang, Ren Yuan, and Dong Zhang were holding a victory banquet and had Yanxiao brought to the feast in his cage.
units.literal: At that time Meng Zhixiang, Ren Yuan, and Dong Zhang were holding a grand drinking feast and had Yanxiao's caged cart brought to the gathering.

units.zh: 知祥問曰：「明公頃自梁朝脫身歸命，才平汴水，節制陝郊，近領前鋒，克平劍外，歸朝之後，授爵冊勳，巨鎮尊官，誰與為競！
units.en: Zhixiang asked him, "You left the Liang, came over to us, helped pacify Bian, governed Shaan, led the vanguard and conquered the lands beyond the passes. Back at court you were ennobled and richly rewarded with the highest posts. Who could have rivaled you?
units.literal: Zhixiang asked: "Your Excellency not long ago escaped from the Liang court and submitted to our dynasty, pacified the Bian waters, governed Shaan and the suburbs, lately led the vanguard and conquered the lands beyond the Sword Pass. After returning to court you were enfeoffed and recorded for merit, given great prefectures and honored offices — who could rival you!

units.zh: 奈何躁憤，自毀功庸，入此檻車，還為鄧艾，深可痛惜，誰肯湣之！」
units.en: Why then let rash anger destroy everything you had won, and end in this cage like Deng Ai of old? It is a bitter waste. Who could pity you now?"
units.literal: Why then impulsive anger, destroying your own achievements, entering this caged cart, becoming again a Deng Ai — deeply to be lamented; who would pity you!"

units.zh: 知祥因手自注杯以飲之。
units.en: Zhixiang filled a cup with his own hand and offered it to him.
units.literal: Zhixiang thereupon personally filled a cup and had him drink.

units.zh: 延孝曰：「自知富貴難消，官職已足。
units.en: Yanxiao said, "I knew that fortune is hard to survive and that my rank was already enough.
units.literal: Yanxiao said: "I knew myself that wealth and honor are hard to bear; my offices were already enough.

units.zh: 然郭崇韜佐命元勳，輔成大業，不動干戈，收獲兩川，自古殊功，但恐不及，一旦何罪，闔門被誅；
units.en: Yet Guo Chongtao was a founding minister who helped build the empire and took both circuits of Shu without a battle — a feat unmatched since antiquity. In a single day, for what crime, was his whole household slaughtered?
units.literal: Yet Guo Chongtao was a founding minister who aided the great enterprise, took the Two Chuan without drawing swords — a singular achievement since antiquity, perhaps unequaled — yet in a single day for what crime was his entire household put to death;

units.zh: 延孝之徒，何保首領。
units.en: How could men like me hope to keep our heads?
units.literal: how could men like Yanxiao preserve their heads?

units.zh: 以此思慮，不敢歸朝，天道相違，一旦至此，亦其命也，夫復何言！」
units.en: That is why I dared not return to court. Heaven turned against me, and in a day I came to this. It was my fate. What more can I say?"
units.literal: With this in mind I dared not return to court. Heaven's way opposed me; in a single day it came to this — that too was my fate. What more is there to say!"

units.zh: 及圜班師，行次鳳翔，中使向延嗣齎詔至，遂誅之。
units.en: When Yuan marched home and reached Fengxiang, the imperial envoy Xiang Yansi arrived with an edict, and Yanxiao was executed.
units.literal: When Yuan withdrew the army and was passing Fengxiang, the imperial envoy Xiang Yansi arrived bearing an edict, and Yanxiao was thereupon executed.

units.zh: 部下懷其首級，瘞於昭應縣民陳暉地。
units.en: His men kept his head and buried it on land belonging to a commoner named Chen Hui in Zhaoying County.
units.literal: His subordinates took his head and buried it on the land of the commoner Chen Hui in Zhaoying County.

units.zh: 天成初，其子發之攜去。
units.en: Early in the Tiancheng era his son disinterred it and took it away.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Tiancheng reign his son dug it up and took it away.

units.zh: 朱守殷，小字會兒。
units.en: Zhu Shouyin, whose childhood name was Huier.
units.literal: Zhu Shouyin — his childhood name was Huier.

units.zh: 莊宗就學，以廝養之役給事左右。
units.en: While Zhuangzong was still a student, Shouyin served him as a groom in his household.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong was studying, he was assigned in the role of groom to serve at his side.

units.zh: 及莊宗即位，為長直軍使，雖列戎行，不聞戰攻。
units.en: When Zhuangzong became emperor, Shouyin was made commander of the Long-Direct Guard. He held military rank but was never known for seeing combat.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he became commander of the Long-Direct Guard. Though listed in the military ranks, he was never known for fighting.

units.zh: 每構人之短長，中於莊宗，漸以心腹受委。
units.en: He constantly played on people's faults and virtues until he had Zhuangzong's ear, and gradually became one of his most trusted intimates.
units.literal: He constantly framed people's faults and merits so as to strike Zhuangzong's heart, and gradually came to be entrusted as an intimate.

units.zh: 河上對壘，稍遷蕃漢馬步都虞候。
units.en: During the standoff on the Yellow River he was promoted to chief adjutant of the combined barbarian and Han cavalry and infantry.
units.literal: When the armies faced each other on the Yellow River, he was gradually promoted to chief adjutant of the barbarian and Han horse and foot forces.

units.zh: 守殷守德勝寨，為梁將王彥章所攻，守殷無備，遂陷南寨。
units.en: Shouyin held Desheng Stockade when the Liang general Wang Yanzhang attacked. Caught unprepared, he lost the southern stockade.
units.literal: Shouyin defended Desheng Stockade and was attacked by the Liang general Wang Yanzhang. Shouyin was unprepared, and the southern stockade fell.

units.zh: 莊宗聞之曰：「駑才大誤予事！」
units.en: Zhuangzong said when he heard the news, "That worthless fool has ruined my campaign!"
units.literal: Zhuangzong heard of it and said: "This incompetent has gravely harmed my affairs!"

units.zh: 因撤北寨，往固楊劉。
units.en: He pulled back from the northern stockade and went to reinforce Yangliu.
units.literal: He therefore withdrew the northern stockade and went to secure Yangliu.

units.zh: 明宗在鄆州，密請以覆軍之罪罪之，莊宗私於腹心，忍而不問。
units.en: Mingzong, then at Yan Prefecture, privately urged that Shouyin be punished for losing the army. Zhuangzong, speaking only with his closest confidants, let the matter pass.
units.literal: Mingzong was at Yan Prefecture and secretly requested that he be punished for the crime of losing the army. Zhuangzong confided in his intimates and bore with it without inquiry.

units.zh: 同光二年，為振武節度使，不之任，仍兼領蕃漢馬步軍。
units.en: In the second year of Tongguang he was appointed military governor of Zhenwu but never took up the post, continuing to command the combined barbarian and Han forces.
units.literal: In the second year of Tongguang he was made military governor of Zhenwu but did not take up the post, still concurrently commanding the barbarian and Han horse and foot forces.

units.zh: 京城初定，內外警巡，恃憑主恩，蔑視勳舊，與景進互相表裏，又強作宿德之態，言語遲緩，自謂沉厚。
units.en: After the capital was secured he took charge of internal and external patrols. Secure in the emperor's favor, he scorned the old meritocrats, worked hand in glove with Jing Jin, and affected the air of a seasoned elder — speaking slowly and calling himself grave and steady.
units.literal: When the capital was first secured he patrolled inside and outside the city. Relying on the ruler's favor, he looked down on meritorious veterans, acted in concert with Jing Jin, and also forced a manner of long-tested virtue — slow of speech, calling himself deep and steady.

units.zh: 及郭從謙犯興教門，步軍始亂，中使急召騎士，守殷按甲不進，莊宗獨領宦官斫射，屢退，而騎軍終不至。
units.en: When Guo Congqian stormed Xingjiao Gate the infantry broke first. Palace envoys urgently summoned the cavalry, but Shouyin held his men back. Zhuangzong fought on alone with his eunuchs, was driven back again and again, and the horsemen never came.
units.literal: When Guo Congqian attacked Xingjiao Gate the foot soldiers first fell into disorder. The palace envoy urgently summoned the horsemen, but Shouyin held his armor and did not advance. Zhuangzong alone led the eunuchs in hacking and shooting, was repeatedly driven back, and the cavalry never arrived.

units.zh: 莊宗既崩，守殷擁眾方在北邙，憩於茂林之下。
units.en: When Zhuangzong died, Shouyin was camped with his troops on North Mang, resting in a wooded grove.
units.literal: After Zhuangzong had died, Shouyin was leading his troops on North Mang and was resting beneath a dense grove.

units.zh: 迨聞凶問，乃入內，選嬪御及珍寶以歸，恣軍士劫掠京都，翌日方定，率諸校迎明宗於東郊。
units.en: Only when word of the death reached him did he enter the palace, seize concubines and treasures, and let his soldiers loot the capital at will. Order was restored only the next day, when he led his officers to welcome Mingzong at the eastern suburb.
units.literal: Only when he heard the news of death did he enter the palace, select palace women and treasures to take away, and let the soldiers plunder the capital at will. The next day order was restored, and he led the commanders to welcome Mingzong at the eastern suburb.

units.zh: 天成初，授河南尹，判六軍諸衛事，加侍中，移汴州節度使。
units.en: Early in the Tiancheng era he was made metropolitan governor of Henan with authority over the Six Armies and palace guards, promoted to Palace Attendant, and transferred to military governor of Bian.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was appointed Metropolitan Governor of Henan, given charge of the Six Armies and palace guards, made Palace Attendant, and transferred as military governor of Bian Prefecture.

units.zh: 車駕將巡幸，外議喧然，初以為平吳，又云製置東諸侯。
units.en: When the emperor prepared to go on tour, rumor ran wild outside the city — first that he meant to pacify Wu, then that he meant to reorganize the eastern lords.
units.literal: When the imperial carriage was about to go on tour, public talk was loud outside: at first it was thought to be pacifying Wu, then it was said to be regulating the eastern feudatories.

units.zh: 守殷乃生雲夢之疑，遂殺都校馬彥超、副使宋敬。
units.en: Shouyin grew suspicious — like the king of Chu who dreamed of Yunmeng — and killed the chief commander Ma Yanchao and the deputy Song Jing.
units.literal: Shouyin then conceived suspicions like those of Yunmeng and thereupon killed the chief commander Ma Yanchao and the deputy Song Jing.

units.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》：守殷將叛，召都指揮使馬彥超與計事，彥超不從，守殷殺之。
units.en: (According to Ouyang Xiu's New History of the Five Dynasties: When Shouyin was plotting rebellion, he summoned the chief commander Ma Yanchao to consult him. Yanchao refused, and Shouyin killed him.
units.literal: (Ouyang's History: When Shouyin was about to rebel, he summoned the chief commander Ma Yanchao to plan with him. Yanchao would not agree, and Shouyin killed him.

units.zh: 明宗憐彥超之死，以其子承祚為洺州長史。）〉
units.en: Mingzong pitied Yanchao and appointed his son Chengzuo long secretary of Luo Prefecture.)〉
units.literal: Mingzong pitied Yanchao's death and made his son Chengzuo long secretary of Luo Prefecture.)〉

units.zh: 守殷驅市人閉壁以叛，明宗途次京水，聞之，親統禁軍，倍程直抵其壘，長圍夾攻，縋城甚眾。
units.en: Shouyin forced the townspeople to shut the gates and rebel. Mingzong was at Jingshui on the road; hearing the news, he led the palace guard himself, marched at double speed to the rebel stronghold, invested it on all sides, and many defenders fled down ropes from the walls.
units.literal: Shouyin drove the townspeople to close the walls and rebel. Mingzong was on the road at Jingshui; when he heard of it he personally led the palace guard, doubled his pace straight to the rebel camp, laid a long siege with attacks from two sides, and many were lowered from the walls on ropes.

units.zh: 守殷力屈，盡殺其族，引頸令左右盡其命。
units.en: When his strength gave out, Shouyin killed every member of his clan, bared his neck, and told his attendants to finish him.
units.literal: Shouyin's strength was exhausted; he slaughtered his entire clan, stretched out his neck, and ordered those at his side to end his life.

units.zh: 王師入城，索其黨，盡誅之。
units.en: The imperial army entered the city, hunted down his followers, and executed them all.
units.literal: The imperial army entered the city, sought out his partisans, and executed them all.

units.zh: 詔鞭守殷屍，梟首懸於都市，滿七日，傳送洛陽。
units.en: An edict ordered Shouyin's corpse flogged and his head displayed in the marketplace. After seven days the head was sent on to Luoyang.
units.literal: An edict ordered Shouyin's corpse to be flogged and his head displayed in the market. After seven days it was sent on to Luoyang.

units.zh: 楊立者，潞州之小校。
units.en: Yang Li was a junior officer in Luzhou.
units.literal: Yang Li was a petty officer of Luzhou.

units.zh: 初事李嗣昭及李繼韜，皆畜養甚厚。
units.en: He had first served Li Sizhao and then Li Jiyao, both of whom treated him with exceptional generosity.
units.literal: He first served Li Sizhao and Li Jiyao, and both raised and supported him very generously.

units.zh: 繼韜被誅，憤憤失誌。
units.en: When Jiyao was executed, Yang Li was bitter and lost heart.
units.literal: When Jiyao was executed, he was resentful and lost his purpose.

units.zh: 同光二年四月，有詔以潞兵三萬人戍涿州，將發，其眾謀曰：「我輩事故使二十年，衣食豐足，未嘗邊塞征行，苟於邊上差跌，白骨何歸？
units.en: In the fourth month of the second year of Tongguang an edict ordered thirty thousand Luzhou troops to garrison Zhuo Prefecture. As they prepared to march, the men plotted among themselves. "We have served our old commissioner for twenty years in comfort and have never fought on the frontier. If we fail out there, where will our bones lie?
units.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Tongguang an edict ordered thirty thousand Luzhou troops to garrison Zhuo Prefecture. As they were about to set out, the men plotted, saying: "We have served the former commissioner for twenty years with ample food and clothing and have never campaigned on the frontier. If we stumble on the border, to what grave will our white bones return?

units.zh: 不如據城自固，事成則富貴耳。」
units.en: Better to hold the city. If we succeed, wealth and rank will follow."
units.literal: Better to hold the city and secure ourselves; if the affair succeeds, then wealth and honor."

units.zh: 因聚徒百餘輩，攻子城東門，城中大擾。
units.en: They gathered more than a hundred men, stormed the east gate of the inner city, and threw the town into chaos.
units.literal: Thereupon they gathered more than a hundred followers, attacked the east gate of the inner city, and threw the city into great disorder.

units.zh: 副使李繼珂及監軍張機祚出奔。
units.en: The deputy Li Jike and the army supervisor Zhang Jizuo fled the city.
units.literal: The deputy Li Jike and the army supervisor Zhang Jizuo fled.

units.zh: 立自稱留後，率軍民上表請旄節。
units.en: Yang Li declared himself acting commissioner and led soldiers and civilians in a memorial requesting formal appointment.
units.literal: Li styled himself acting commissioner and led the soldiers and people in submitting a memorial requesting the staff of command.

units.zh: 莊宗怒，命明宗與李紹真攻討，一月拔之，生擒立及其同惡十餘人，送於闕下，皆磔於市。
units.en: Zhuangzong was furious and ordered Mingzong and Li Shaozhen to attack. Within a month the city fell. Yang Li and more than ten of his accomplices were taken alive, sent to the capital, and dismembered in the marketplace.
units.literal: Zhuangzong was angry and ordered Mingzong and Li Shaozhen to attack. In one month the city was taken; Li and more than ten of his fellow evildoers were captured alive, sent to the capital, and all dismembered in the market.

units.zh: 潞州城峻而隍深，攻立輒敢據之，莊宗因茲詔諸道撤防城之備焉。
units.en: Luzhou's walls were high and its moat deep, yet Yang Li had dared to hold it. Zhuangzong therefore ordered every circuit to dismantle its outer defensive works.
units.literal: Luzhou's walls were high and its moat deep, yet Li dared to hold it against attack. Zhuangzong therefore issued an edict to all circuits to dismantle defensive preparations on city walls.

units.zh: 竇廷琬者，世為青州牙將，梁祖擢置左右。
units.en: Dou Tingwan came from a family of military aides in Qing Prefecture. Emperor Taizu of Liang brought him into his personal service.
units.literal: Dou Tingwan — for generations his family were military aides of Qing Prefecture; the Founder of Liang promoted him to his personal attendants.

units.zh: 同光初，為復州遊奕使，奸盜屏跡，曆貝州刺史。
units.en: Early in Tongguang he served as patrol commissioner of Fu Prefecture, where bandits and thieves disappeared from his district. He later became prefect of Bei.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was patrol commissioner of Fu Prefecture; thieves and robbers vanished from his jurisdiction, and he successively served as prefect of Bei Prefecture.

units.zh: 未幾，請製置慶州鹽池，逐年出絹十萬匹，米十萬斛，遂以廷琬為慶州防禦使。
units.en: Before long he petitioned to take charge of the salt ponds of Qing Prefecture, pledging an annual yield of one hundred thousand bolts of silk and one hundred thousand hu of grain. Tingwan was then appointed defender of Qing.
units.literal: Before long he requested to administer the salt ponds of Qing Prefecture, with annual output of one hundred thousand bolts of silk and one hundred thousand hu of grain, and thereupon Tingwan was made defender of Qing Prefecture.

units.zh: 俾製置之，由是嚴刑峻法，屢撓邊人。
units.en: Once put in charge, he ruled with harsh punishments and severe laws and repeatedly oppressed the frontier population.
units.literal: He was ordered to administer it, and from this employed harsh punishments and severe laws, repeatedly harassing the frontier people.

units.zh: 課利不集，詔移任於金州。
units.en: When the expected revenues failed to materialize, an edict transferred him to Jin Prefecture.
units.literal: Tribute profits did not accumulate; an edict transferred his appointment to Jin Prefecture.

units.zh: 廷琬據慶州叛，詔邠州節度使李敬周率兵討平之，夷其族。
units.en: Tingwan rebelled and held Qing Prefecture. An edict sent Li Jingzhou, military governor of Bin, to suppress him. When the revolt was crushed, his entire clan was wiped out.
units.literal: Tingwan held Qing Prefecture in rebellion. An edict ordered the military governor of Bin Li Jingzhou to lead troops to suppress and pacify him, and his clan was exterminated.

units.zh: 張虔釗，遼州人也。
units.en: Zhang Qianzhao was a native of Liao Prefecture.
units.literal: Zhang Qianzhao was a man of Liao Prefecture.

units.zh: 〈（《九國志》云：虔釗，遼州榆社人。
units.en: (According to the Annals of the Nine States: Qianzhao was from Yushe in Liao Prefecture.
units.literal: (Annals of the Nine States says: Qianzhao was a man of Yushe in Liao Prefecture.

units.zh: 父簡，唐檢校尚書左僕射。）〉
units.en: His father Jian had served as Honorary Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat under Tang.)〉
units.literal: His father Jian was Tang's Honorary Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.)〉

units.zh: 初為太原牙校，以武勇聞於流輩，武皇、莊宗之世，累補左右突騎軍使。
units.en: He began as a military aide at Taiyuan and won a reputation for courage among his peers. Under Emperor Wuzong and Zhuangzong he rose repeatedly to command the Left and Right Flying Cavalry.
units.literal: At first he was a military aide at Taiyuan; his martial valor was known among his peers. In the reigns of Emperor Wuzong and Zhuangzong he was repeatedly appointed commander of the Left and Right Flying Cavalry.

units.zh: 〈（《九國志》：莊宗嘗以偏師取鎮陽，命虔釗率騎為先鋒，屢挫賊銳，遂陷其城。）〉
units.en: (According to the Annals of the Nine States: Zhuangzong once took Zhenyang with a detached column and made Qianzhao lead the cavalry vanguard. Qianzhao repeatedly broke the enemy's best troops and finally captured the city.)〉
units.literal: (Annals of the Nine States: Zhuangzong once took Zhenyang with a detached force, ordered Qianzhao to lead the cavalry as vanguard, repeatedly blunted the enemy's sharp edge, and finally stormed the city.)〉

units.zh: 明宗素聞虔釗有將帥才，及即位，擢為護駕親軍都指揮使，領春州刺史。
units.en: Mingzong had long heard of Qianzhao's gifts as a commander. When he took the throne he made Qianzhao chief commander of the imperial guard and prefect of Chun.
units.literal: Mingzong had long heard that Qianzhao had talent as a general. When he took the throne he promoted him to chief commander of the imperial guard cavalry and made him prefect of Chun Prefecture.

units.zh: 天成中，與諸將圍王都於中山，大敗契丹於嘉山之下，及定州平，以功授滄州節度使。
units.en: During Tiancheng he joined other generals in besieging Wang Du at Zhongshan and routed the Khitan below Mount Jia. When Ding Prefecture fell, he was rewarded with the military governorship of Cang.
units.literal: During Tiancheng he joined the generals in besieging Wang Du at Zhongshan, greatly defeated the Khitan below Mount Jia, and when Ding Prefecture was pacified was made military governor of Cang Prefecture for his merit.

units.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》：虔釗鎮滄州日，因亢旱民饑，發廩賑之，方上聞，帝甚嘉獎。
units.en: (According to Miscellaneous Tales from Northern Dreams: While Qianzhao governed Cang, a severe drought brought famine. He opened the granaries to feed the people. When the report reached court, the emperor praised him warmly.
units.literal: (Miscellaneous Tales from Northern Dreams: When Qianzhao governed Cang Prefecture, because of severe drought the people were hungry; he opened the granaries to relieve them. The report had just reached the throne when the emperor greatly praised and rewarded him.

units.zh: 他日秋成，倍鬥征斂，朝論鄙之。）〉
units.en: Later, after the autumn harvest, he doubled the tax levies, and court opinion turned against him.)〉
units.literal: Another day when the autumn harvest came in, he doubled the levies; court opinion despised him.)〉

units.zh: 移鎮徐州。
units.en: He was transferred to Xuzhou.
units.literal: He was transferred to garrison Xuzhou.

units.zh: 長興中，為山南西道節度使兼西面馬步軍都部署。
units.en: During Changxing he served as military governor of Shannan West Circuit and chief deployer of the western horse and foot armies.
units.literal: In Changxing he was military governor of Shannan West Circuit and concurrently chief deployer of the western horse and foot armies.

units.zh: 及末帝起於鳳翔，閔帝詔令虔釗帥部兵會王師於岐下。
units.en: When the Last Emperor rose at Fengxiang, Emperor Min ordered Qianzhao to lead his troops and join the imperial army at Qi.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor rose at Fengxiang, Emperor Min ordered Qianzhao to lead his troops to join the imperial army below Qi.

units.zh: 洎西師俱變，虔釗憤惋，退歸興元，因與洋州節度使孫漢韶俱送款於蜀。
units.en: When the western armies all turned, Qianzhao withdrew to Xingyuan in anger and grief. He and Sun Hanzhao, military governor of Yang, then both submitted to Shu.
units.literal: When the western armies all mutinied, Qianzhao was resentful and grieved, withdrew to Xingyuan, and thereupon he and the military governor of Yang Prefecture Sun Hanzhao both sent pledges of submission to Shu.

units.zh: 孟知祥待之尤厚，偽授本鎮節度使，俾知祥坐獲山南之地，由虔釗之故也。
units.en: Meng Zhixiang treated him with exceptional generosity and invested him as military governor of his former circuit. It was largely through Qianzhao that Zhixiang gained the lands of Shannan without a fight.
units.literal: Meng Zhixiang treated him with especial generosity and falsely invested him as military governor of his own circuit. That Zhixiang easily gained the lands of Shannan was owing to Qianzhao.

units.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》：入蜀，取人產業，黷貨無厭，蜀民怨之。）〉
units.en: (According to Miscellaneous Tales from Northern Dreams: Once in Shu he seized people's property, took bribes without limit, and earned the hatred of the Shu populace.)〉
units.literal: (Miscellaneous Tales from Northern Dreams: After entering Shu he seized people's estates, was insatiably corrupt, and the people of Shu resented him.)〉

units.zh: 孟昶嗣偽位，加檢校太師、兼中書令。
units.en: When Meng Chang succeeded to the Shu throne, Qianzhao was made Honorary Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: When Meng Chang succeeded to the false throne, Qianzhao was made Honorary Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 晉開運末，蜀人聞契丹入洛，令虔釗率眾數萬，將寇秦、雍。
units.en: Late in the Kaiyun era of Jin, when Shu heard that the Khitan had entered Luoyang, Chang ordered Qianzhao to lead tens of thousands against Qin and Yong.
units.literal: At the end of Kaiyun of Jin, the Shu people heard the Khitan had entered Luoyang and ordered Qianzhao to lead tens of thousands to invade Qin and Yong.

units.zh: 俄聞漢高祖已定中原，虔釗無功而退。
units.en: Soon word came that Emperor Gaozu of Han had secured the Central Plains, and Qianzhao withdrew without accomplishing anything.
units.literal: Soon they heard Emperor Gaozu of Han had secured the Central Plains; Qianzhao withdrew without achievement.

units.zh: 〈（《九國志》云：曆左右匡聖馬步軍都指揮使，出為昭武軍節度使。
units.en: (According to the Annals of the Nine States: He had served in turn as chief commander of the Left and Right Kuangsheng armies and then as military governor of Zhaowu.
units.literal: (Annals of the Nine States says: He successively served as chief commander of the Left and Right Kuangsheng horse and foot armies and went out as military governor of Zhaowu Army.

units.zh: 及漢祖即位，乃移鎮梁州，以觀朝廷之變。
units.en: When the Han founder took the throne, he was moved to Liang Prefecture to watch how events at court would unfold.
units.literal: When the Han founder took the throne, he was transferred to garrison Liang Prefecture to observe changes at court.

units.zh: 會晉昌軍節度使趙匡讚、鳳翔節度使侯益俱謀歸蜀，遂以虔釗為北面行營招討使，應接經營。
units.en: When Zhao Kuangzan of Jinchang and Hou Yi of Fengxiang both plotted to defect to Shu, Qianzhao was made northern-campaign pacification commissioner to coordinate the effort.
units.literal: It happened that the military governor of Jinchang Army Zhao Kuangzan and the military governor of Fengxiang Hou Yi both plotted to submit to Shu; thereupon Qianzhao was made northern-campaign pacification commissioner to receive and manage affairs.

units.zh: 俄而趙匡讚、侯益請昶出師，掠定三秦，因命虔釗與韓保貞等總師五萬出散關，雄武軍節度使何重建出隴右，奉鑾肅衛都虞候李廷珪出子午穀，會於雍州。
units.en: Soon Zhao and Hou urged Chang to march and seize the Three Qin. Chang ordered Qianzhao and Han Baozhen to lead fifty thousand men through San Pass, He Chongjian of Xiongwu to advance through Longyou, and Li Tinggui of the Imperial Escort to march through Ziwu Valley. All were to converge on Yong.
units.literal: Soon Zhao Kuangzan and Hou Yi requested that Chang send troops to raid and secure the Three Qin. Thereupon he ordered Qianzhao with Han Baozhen and others to command fifty thousand troops out through San Pass, the military governor of Xiongwu Army He Chongjian out through Longyou, and the chief adjutant of the Imperial Escort Guard Li Tinggui out through Ziwu Valley, to meet at Yong Prefecture.

units.zh: 廷珪始出子午穀，聞匡讚為王景崇所逼，棄城自拔東去，遂先退師。
units.en: Tinggui had barely left Ziwu Valley when he learned that Kuangzan was being driven by Wang Jingchong, abandoned his position, and fled east. He was the first to withdraw.
units.literal: Tinggui had just emerged from Ziwu Valley when he heard Kuangzan was pressed by Wang Jingchong, abandoned the city and fled east on his own, and thereupon first withdrew his army.

units.zh: 時虔釗、福誠、保貞師次陳倉，謀不相葉，而侯益聞匡讚已去，廷珪班師，亦誠款中變，閉壘不出。
units.en: By then Qianzhao, Fucheng, and Baozhen had halted at Chencang and could not agree among themselves. Hou Yi heard that Kuangzan was gone and Tinggui had withdrawn, changed his mind about submitting, and shut himself behind his walls.
units.literal: At that time the armies of Qianzhao, Fucheng, and Baozhen halted at Chencang and would not cooperate with one another. Hou Yi heard Kuangzan had gone, Tinggui had withdrawn his army, and his own pledge of sincerity changed midway; he closed his ramparts and would not come out.

units.zh: 司天監趙廷樞累以雲氣不利為諷，保貞乃與福誠率所部取隴州道，會重建歸蜀，虔釗留寶雞，以勢孤不可深入，遂班師。）〉
units.en: The director of the Astronomical Bureau, Zhao Tingshu, repeatedly warned that the omens were unfavorable. Baozhen and Fucheng then led their men toward Long Prefecture. When He Chongjian returned to Shu, Qianzhao held Baoji but, finding his force too isolated to advance, withdrew.)〉
units.literal: The Director of the Astronomical Bureau Zhao Tingshu repeatedly used unfavorable cloud signs as admonition. Baozhen then led his troops with Fucheng by the Long Prefecture route; when Chongjian returned to Shu, Qianzhao remained at Baoji. Seeing his position isolated and that he could not advance deeply, he thereupon withdrew his army.)〉

units.zh: 行至興州，感憤而卒。
units.en: He reached Xing Prefecture and died there, overcome with grief and anger.
units.literal: Reaching Xing Prefecture, he died of grief and indignation.

units.zh: 楊彥溫，汴州人，本梁朝之小校也。
units.en: Yang Yanwen was a native of Bian and had begun as a junior officer in the Liang army.
units.literal: Yang Yanwen was a man of Bian; originally a petty officer of the Liang court.

units.zh: 莊宗朝，累遷裨將。
units.en: Under Zhuangzong he rose repeatedly to deputy commander.
units.literal: In Zhuangzong's reign he was repeatedly promoted to deputy general.

units.zh: 天成中，為河中副指揮使，及末帝鎮河中，尤善待之，因奏為衙內都指揮使。
units.en: During Tiancheng he served as deputy commander at Hezhong. When the Last Emperor governed there, he treated Yanwen with special favor and had him appointed chief commander of the inner guards.
units.literal: During Tiancheng he was deputy commander at Hezhong. When the Last Emperor governed Hezhong he was especially well treated, and thereupon memorialized him as chief commander of the inner guards.

units.zh: 長興元年四月，乘末帝閱馬於黃龍莊，據城謀叛。
units.en: In the fourth month of the first year of Changxing, while the Last Emperor was inspecting horses at Yellow Dragon Manor, Yanwen seized the city and rebelled.
units.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Changxing, while the Last Emperor was inspecting horses at Yellow Dragon Manor, Yanwen seized the city and plotted rebellion.

units.zh: 末帝遣人詰之曰：「吾善待汝，何苦為叛？」
units.en: The Last Emperor sent a messenger to demand, "I have treated you well. Why turn rebel?"
units.literal: The Last Emperor sent someone to question him, saying: "I have treated you well — why must you rebel?"

units.zh: 彥溫報曰：「某非敢負恩，緣奉樞密院宣頭，令某拒命，請相公但歸朝廷。」
units.en: Yanwen replied, "I do not mean to repay your kindness with treachery. I am acting on an order from the Bureau of Military Affairs telling me to resist you. I ask only that you return to court."
units.literal: Yanwen replied: "I do not dare betray your kindness. It is because I received an order from the Bureau of Military Affairs directing me to refuse your command. I ask that Your Lordship simply return to court."

units.zh: 數日，詔末帝歸朝。
units.en: Within days an edict ordered the Last Emperor back to court.
units.literal: After several days an edict ordered the Last Emperor to return to court.

units.zh: 明宗疑其詐，不欲興兵，授彥溫絳州刺史。
units.en: Mingzong suspected a ruse and refused to send troops. He appointed Yanwen prefect of Jiang.
units.literal: Mingzong suspected fraud and did not wish to raise troops; he appointed Yanwen prefect of Jiang Prefecture.

units.zh: 安重誨堅請出師，即命西京留守索自通、侍衛步軍指揮使藥彥稠等帥兵攻之。
units.en: An Chonghui insisted on military action. Mingzong ordered Suo Zhitong, military governor of the western capital, Yao Yanchou, commander of the palace guard infantry, and others to attack.
units.literal: An Chonghui firmly requested troops be sent and immediately ordered the western capital's military governor Suo Zhitong, the commander of the palace guard infantry Yao Yanchou, and others to lead troops against him.

units.zh: 五日而拔，自閉門及敗，凡十三日。
units.en: The city fell in five days. From the closing of the gates to defeat, the affair lasted thirteen days.
units.literal: The city was taken in five days; from closing the gates to defeat, thirteen days in all.

units.zh: 初，彥稠出師，明宗戒之曰：「與朕生致彥溫，吾將自訊之。」
units.en: Before Yao Yanchou marched out, Mingzong warned him, "Bring Yanwen to me alive. I mean to question him myself."
units.literal: At first, when Yao Yanchou set out, Mingzong admonished him: "Bring Yanwen to me alive; I will question him myself."

units.zh: 及收城，斬首傳送，明宗深怒彥稠等。
units.en: When the city fell, they beheaded Yanwen and sent his head to court. Mingzong was furious with Yao Yanchou and his officers.
units.literal: When the city was taken, his head was cut off and sent on; Mingzong was deeply angry with Yao Yanchou and the others.

units.zh: 時議者以當時四海恬然，五兵載戢，蒲非邊郡，近在國門，而彥溫安敢狂悖。
units.en: Contemporaries noted that the realm was at peace and arms had been laid aside. Pu was no frontier post but lay at the capital's doorstep. How could Yanwen dare such madness?
units.literal: Commentators of the time held that the four seas were then tranquil and weapons were laid aside; Pu was not a frontier prefecture but lay close to the capital gates — how dared Yanwen be so reckless and perverse?

units.zh: 皆以為安重誨方弄國權，尤忌末帝之名，故巧作窺圖，究莫能傾陷也。
units.en: Most believed that An Chonghui, who was then wielding state power and especially feared the Last Emperor's standing, had engineered the affair as a probe — yet in the end failed to bring him down.
units.literal: All believed that An Chonghui was then manipulating state power and especially feared the Last Emperor's reputation; therefore he craftily devised a scheme of probing, yet in the end could not overthrow him.

units.zh: 彥溫愚昧，為人所嗾，故滅其族焉。
units.en: Yanwen was a fool used by others, and for that his whole clan was destroyed.
units.literal: Yanwen was foolish and was incited by others; therefore his clan was exterminated.

units.zh: 史臣曰：《春秋傳》云：「夫不令之臣，天下之所惡也。」
units.en: The historiographer remarks: The Zuo Commentary says, "An unworthy minister is hated by all under Heaven."
units.literal: The historiographer says: The Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: "An unworthy minister is what all under Heaven detests."

units.zh: 故不復較其優劣焉。
units.en: I therefore do not weigh their relative merits and faults.
units.literal: Therefore I do not again compare their relative merits and faults.

units.zh: 唯虔釗因避地以偷生，彥溫乃為人之所嗾，比諸叛臣，亦可矜也。
units.en: Only Qianzhao, who fled to preserve his life, and Yanwen, who was driven by others, deserve some pity when set beside the other rebels in this chapter.
units.literal: Only Qianzhao, because he fled the land to preserve his life, and Yanwen, because he was incited by others — compared with other rebel ministers, may also be pitied.

units.zh: 帝內殿食次，從馬直指揮使郭從謙自本營率所部抽戈露刃，至興教門大呼，與黃甲兩軍引弓射興教門。
units.en: While the Emperor dined in the inner palace, Guo Congqian, commander of the Direct Horse Corps, led his troops from camp with drawn swords to Xingjiao Gate, shouting; the Yellow Armor armies shot at the gate.
units.literal: While the Emperor was at a meal in the inner hall, Guo Congqian, commander of the Direct Horse Corps, led his men from camp with bared blades to Xingjiao Gate shouting; with the Yellow Armor two armies he drew bows and shot at Xingjiao Gate.

units.zh: 《東都事略·符彥卿傳》云：郭從謙之亂，莊宗左右皆引去，惟彥卿力戰，殺十餘人。
units.en: The 《Outline of the Eastern Capital · Fu Yanqing Biography》 says that in Guo Congqian's revolt Zhuangzong's attendants all fled; only Yanqing fought hard and killed more than ten men.
units.literal: The 《Outline of the Eastern Capital · Fu Yanqing Biography》 says: at Guo Congqian's rebellion Zhuangzong's attendants all withdrew; only Yanqing fought fiercely and killed more than ten.

units.zh: 帝聞其變，自宮中率諸王近衛禦之，逐亂兵出門。
units.en: Hearing the mutiny, the Emperor led princes and palace guards out to fight and drove the rebels from the gate.
units.literal: The Emperor heard of the mutiny, led princes and close guards from the palace to resist, and drove the rebel troops out the gate.

units.zh: 既而焚興教門，緣城而入，登宮牆歡噪，帝御親軍格鬥，殺亂兵數百。
units.en: They soon burned Xingjiao Gate, scaled the wall, and cheered from the palace ramparts; the Emperor fought with his personal guard and killed hundreds of rebels.
units.literal: Soon they burned Xingjiao Gate, climbed in along the wall, mounted the palace ramparts shouting in joy; the Emperor led his personal guard in hand-to-hand combat and killed several hundred rebels.

units.zh: 六月甲辰，以金紫光祿大夫、檢校司徒、歙州刺史朱令德為忠武軍節度觀察留後。
units.en: On jiachen in the sixth month, Zhu Lingde of She, Purple-Gold Grand Master and honorary Situ, was made Zhongwu observation commissioner.
units.literal: On jiachen in the sixth month, Purple-Gold Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, honorary Situ, and She prefect Zhu Lingde was made Zhongwu Army observation and retention commissioner.

units.zh: 帝遣西京留守索自通、侍衛步軍都指揮使藥彥稠等攻之，仍授彥溫絳州刺史，冀誘而擒之也。
units.en: Mingzong sent Suo Zitong, Yao Yanchou, and others against him while naming Yanwen Jiang prefect to lure his surrender.
units.literal: The Emperor dispatched Western Capital regent Suo Zitong, commander-in-chief of the Palace Guard foot army Yao Yanchou, and others to attack him, still appointing Yanwen prefect of Jiang prefecture, hoping to lure and capture him.

units.zh: 癸丑，索自通、藥彥稠等奏，收復河中，斬楊彥溫，傳首來獻。
units.en: On guichou Suo Zitong and Yao Yanchou reported recovering Hedong, beheading Yang Yanwen, and sending his head.
units.literal: On guichou, Suo Zitong, Yao Yanchou, and others memorialized that Hedong had been recovered, Yang Yanwen beheaded, and his head sent in offering.

units.zh: 初，彥稠出師，帝戒之曰：「與朕生致彥溫，吾將自訊之。」
units.en: Before the march Mingzong warned Yanchou: "Bring Yanwen alive—I will question him myself."
units.literal: Earlier, when Yanchou marched out, the Emperor warned him: "Bring Yanwen alive to me—I will question him myself."

units.zh: 及收城，斬首傳送，帝怒彥稠等。
units.en: They sent his head instead and Mingzong was angry with Yanchou and the others.
units.literal: When the city was taken, the head was cut off and sent; the Emperor was angry at Yanchou and the others.

units.zh: 繼岌既受都統之命，以梁漢顒充中軍馬步都虞候兼馬步軍都指揮使，張廷蘊為中軍步軍都指揮使，牛景章充中軍左廂馬軍都指揮使，沈斌充中軍右廂馬軍都指揮使，卓瑰充中軍左廂步軍都指揮使，王贄充中軍右廂步軍都指揮使，供奉官李從襲充中軍馬步軍都監，高品李廷安、呂知柔充魏王衙通謁。
units.en: Jiji named Liang Hanyong central horse-and-foot chief, Zhang Tingyun foot chief, Niu Jingzhang and Shen Bin wing horse chiefs, Zhuo Gui and Wang Zan wing foot chiefs, Li Congxi monitor, and Li Ting'an and Lü Zhirou ushers.
units.literal: Jiji having received the overall command, Liang Hanyong was made chief of central horse and foot and overall horse-and-foot commander; Zhang Tingyun was central foot commander; Niu Jingzhang was left-wing horse commander; Shen Bin was right-wing horse commander; Zhuo Gui was left-wing foot commander; Wang Zan was right-wing foot commander; Palace Attendant Li Congxi was overall monitor of central horse and foot; senior attendants Li Ting'an and Lü Zhirou were Prince of Wei gate ushers.

units.zh: 九月辛卯朔，河陽奏，黃河漲一丈五尺。
units.en: On the xinmao new moon of the ninth month Heyang said the Yellow River was up 1.5 zhang.
units.literal: Ninth month, xinmao new moon: Heyang reported the Yellow River had risen one zhang five chi.

units.zh: 己丑，以振武軍節度使、權安義留後、檢校太傅、平章事李存霸為潞州節度使，以捧日都指揮使、鄭州防禦使李紹琛為陝州節度使，以成德軍馬步軍都指揮使、右監門衛大將軍毛璋為華州節度使。
units.en: On jichou Cunba took Luzhou, Li Shaochen Shanzhou, and Mao Zhang Huazhou.
units.literal: On jichou Zhenwu military commissioner, acting Anyi regent, Grand Mentor, and chief minister Li Cunba was made Luzhou military commissioner; Sun-Rising commander and Zhengzhou defender Li Shaochen was made Shanzhou military commissioner; Chengde horse-and-foot commander and Right Gate Guard general Mao Zhang was made Huazhou military commissioner.

units.zh: 丙寅，以西面行營馬軍都指揮使、檢校太保、鄭州刺史、充本州防禦使王彥章為檢校太傅。
units.en: On bingyin, Wang Yanzhang, Western Line horse commander, honorary Grand Guardian, and Zheng prefect and defense commissioner, was promoted to honorary Grand Mentor.
units.literal: On bingyin, Western Line camp horse commander, honorary Grand Guardian, Zheng prefect, and Zheng defense commissioner Wang Yanzhang was made honorary Grand Mentor.

units.zh: 十二月，晉王自太原復至魏州。
units.en: In the twelfth month the Prince of Jin returned from Taiyuan to Weizhou.
units.literal: In the twelfth month the Prince of Jin came again from Taiyuan to Weizhou.

units.zh: 壬午，以前蔚州刺史張溫為振武留後，以左右廂突陣指揮使康義誠為汾州刺史，以左右廂馬軍都指揮使索自通為忻州刺史。
units.en: On renwu, Zhang Wen, former prefect of Weizhou, was made acting military commissioner of Zhenwu; Kang Yicheng, commander of the left and right wing assault formations, was made prefect of Fenzhou; and Suo Zitong, cavalry commander-in-chief of the left and right wings, was made prefect of Xinzhou.
units.literal: On renwu, former Weizhou prefect Zhang Wen was made Zhenwu acting military commissioner; left-and-right wing assault-array commander Kang Yicheng was made Fenzhou prefect; left-and-right wing cavalry commander Suo Zitong was made Xinzhou prefect.

units.zh: 偽六軍使王宗弼報，王衍舉家遷於西宅，宗弼權稱西川兵馬留後；
units.en: The Shu Six Armies commissioner Wang Zongbi reported that Wang Yan had moved his household to the western residence and Zongbi styled himself acting western Shu army retention commissioner;
units.literal: The Shu Six Armies commissioner Wang Zongbi reported that Wang Yan had moved his whole household to the western residence and Zongbi provisionally styled himself western Shu army-and-horse retention commissioner;

units.zh: 〈（《九國誌·王宗弼傳》：唐師陷鳳州，衍遣三招討屯三泉以拒唐師，未戰，三招討俱遁走，因令宗弼守綿穀而誅三招討，宗弼遂與三招討同送款於魏王。
units.en: (The 《Nine States Institutes · Wang Zongbi》 says when Tang took Feng, Yan sent three campaign commanders to Sanquan; before battle all three fled; Yan ordered Zongbi to hold Mian Valley and killed the three commanders; Zongbi then with them submitted to the Prince of Wei.
units.literal: (The 《Nine States Institutes · Wang Zongbi Biography》: when Tang troops took Fengzhou, Yan dispatched the three campaign commanders to camp at Sanquan to resist Tang; before battle all three campaign commanders fled; he then ordered Zongbi to hold Mian Valley and executed the three campaign commanders; Zongbi thereupon with the three campaign commanders together sent allegiance to the Prince of Wei.

units.zh: 十一月庚寅朔，帝幸壽安，號慟於坤陵。
units.en: On the gengyin new moon of the eleventh month Cunxu visited Shou'an and wailed at Kun Mausoleum.
units.literal: Eleventh month, gengyin new moon: the Emperor visited Shou'an and wailed at Kun Mausoleum.

units.zh: 又報偽樞密使宋光嗣景潤澄、宣徽使李周輅歐陽晃同有異謀，惑亂蜀主，已梟斬訖。
units.en: he also reported that Shu privy commissioners Song Guangsi and Jing Runcheng, and Xuanhui commissioners Li Zhoulu and Ouyang Huang, alike had plotted, confused the Shu ruler, and had already been beheaded and displayed.
units.literal: he also reported that Shu privy commissioners Song Guangsi and Jing Runcheng, and Xuanhui commissioners Li Zhoulu and Ouyang Huang, alike harbored divergent plots, confused the Shu ruler, and had already been beheaded and displayed.

units.zh: 乃還成都，斬宋光嗣等，函首送於魏王，遷衍及母妻於西宮。）〉
units.en: He returned to Chengdu, killed Song Guangsi and the rest, sent their heads to the Prince of Wei, and moved Yan, his mother, and his wife to the western palace.)〉
units.literal: He then returned to Chengdu, beheaded Song Guangsi and the rest, sent their heads in boxes to the Prince of Wei, and moved Yan and his mother and wife to the western palace.)〉

units.zh: 鄧艾修淮陽、百尺二渠，通淮、潁、大治諸陂于潁之南，穿渠三百餘裏，溉田二萬頃。
units.en: Deng Ai repaired the Huaiyang and Baichi canals, linking the Huai and Ying and major reservoirs south of the Ying with canals over 300 li long, irrigating 20,000 qing.
units.literal: Deng Ai repaired the Huaiyang and Baichi canals, connecting the Huai, Ying, and great reservoirs south of the Ying, cutting canals more than 300 li and irrigating 20,000 qing of fields.

units.zh: 元行欽請車駕幸汴州，帝將發京師，遣中官向延嗣馳詔所在誅蜀主王衍，仍夷其族。
units.en: Yuan Xingqin asked Cunxu to go to Bian; as he was about to leave the capital he sent Xiang Yansi with a flying edict to execute Wang Yan and exterminate his clan.
units.literal: Yuan Xingqin asked that the imperial carriage go to Bianzhou; the Emperor was about to set out from the capital and sent a palace official, Xiang Yansi, with a flying edict to the place to execute Shu ruler Wang Yan and still exterminate his clan.

units.zh: 會末帝鎮其地，阮稍狎之。
units.en: When the Last Emperor governed the region, Ruan grew somewhat familiar with him.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor governed that region, Ruan grew somewhat familiar with him.

units.zh: 天成中，唐末帝出鎮河中，暠於路左迎謁，求事軍門，末帝愛之，使治賓客。
units.en: During Tiancheng, when the Last Emperor of Tang went out to govern Hezhong, Gao met him at the roadside and sought service at headquarters. The Last Emperor took a liking to him and put him in charge of guests.
units.literal: During Tiancheng, when the Last Emperor of Tang went out to govern Hezhong, Gao met him at the roadside and sought service at headquarters. The Last Emperor took a liking to him and had him manage guests.

units.zh: 末帝嗣位，以阮為趙州刺史。
units.en: When the Last Emperor succeeded to the throne, he appointed Ruan prefect of Zhao.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor succeeded to the throne, he appointed Ruan prefect of Zhao.

units.zh: 及末帝登極，歷南北院宣徽使，尋與趙延壽同為樞密使。
units.en: When the Last Emperor ascended the throne, Gao served successively as commissioner of the southern and northern palace secretariat bureaus, and soon shared the post of confidential commissioner with Zhao Yanshou.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor ascended the throne, Gao served successively as commissioner of the southern and northern bureaus of the Palace Secretariat, and soon shared the post of confidential commissioner with Zhao Yanshou.

units.zh: 〈（《九國誌·李仁罕傳》：夏魯奇稟朝廷之命，繕治甲兵，將圖蜀，孟知祥與董璋謀先取魯奇，令仁罕攻遂州。）〉
units.en: (From the Biography of Li Renhan in the Jiuguo Zhi: Xia Luqi obeyed the court's orders, repaired arms and armor, and prepared to move against Shu. Meng Zhixiang and Dong Zhang plotted to strike him first and ordered Renhan to attack Suizhou.)〉
units.literal: (From the Biography of Li Renhan in the Jiuguo Zhi: Xia Luqi received the court's orders, repaired armor and weapons, and planned to strike Shu; Meng Zhixiang and Dong Zhang plotted first to take Luqi and ordered Renhan to attack Suizhou.)〉

units.zh: 〈（《九國誌·李廷珪傳》：周師攻秦、鳳，以廷珪為北路行營都統，高彥儔、呂彥珂為招討。
units.en: (Jiuguo Zhi, biography of Li Tinggui: When Zhou attacked Qin and Feng, Tinggui was named northern route commander, with Gao Yanchou and Lü Yanke as pacification commissioners.
units.literal: (Jiuguo Zhi, Biography of Li Tinggui: When Zhou troops attacked Qin and Feng, Tinggui was made overall commander of the northern route field army, and Gao Yanchou and Lü Yanke were made pacification commissioners.

units.zh: 廷珪遣先鋒指揮使李進以兵據馬嶺，分兵出斜谷，營於白澗，將腹背以攻周師；
units.en: Tinggui sent vanguard commander Li Jin to hold Maling, detached troops through Xiegu pass, and encamped at Baijian to attack the Zhou from front and rear;
units.literal: Tinggui sent vanguard commander Li Jin with troops to hold Maling, divided troops to exit Xiegu, and encamped at Baijian, intending to attack Zhou troops from front and rear;

units.zh: 丙申，潞州小校楊立據城叛，以李嗣源為招討使，陝州留後李紹真為副，率師以討之。
units.en: On bingshen Yang Li, a Luzhou junior officer, rebelled and held the city; Li Siyuan was made pacification commissioner with Li Shaozhen of Shanzhou as deputy to march against him.
units.literal: On bingshen, Luzhou junior officer Yang Li seized the city in rebellion; Li Siyuan was made pacification commissioner, Shaanzhou acting commissioner Li Shaozhen deputy, and they led troops to attack him.
